title: What is the rapture of the church?
dek: Biblical meaning, timing, and readiness — what Scripture says about believers being caught up to meet the Lord, and why no one is given the day.
body:
The rapture of the church is the event described in 1 Thessalonians 4, in which believers in Jesus Christ — those who have died and those still living — are caught up together to meet the Lord in the air at His return. Scripture gives no date for it and instructs believers to be ready rather than to calculate.

## What is the rapture of the church?

The rapture is the catching up of believers to meet Christ. The passage it comes from is this:

> For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.
> — 1 Thessalonians 4:16–17, KJV

The English word "rapture" does not appear in the Bible. It comes from *raptura*, related to the Latin verb used in the fourth-century Vulgate translation of this verse, which renders the Greek *harpazō* — to seize, snatch, or carry off suddenly. The same Greek verb is used when Philip is carried away after baptising the Ethiopian official (Acts 8:39).

So the term is a description drawn from the passage rather than a biblical title. The event described has three parts: Christ descends, the dead in Christ rise first, and living believers are caught up with them.

## What does the Bible say about the rapture?

Two further passages carry most of the weight. Paul describes the same moment to the Corinthians, adding what happens to the body:

> We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed, In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump.
> — 1 Corinthians 15:51–52, KJV

This is where the idea of transformation comes from. Paul's argument is that mortal bodies are not simply relocated but changed — a point he develops by saying corruption must put on incorruption (1 Corinthians 15:53).

Jesus Christ Himself gave the promise that these passages assume:

> I will come again, and receive you unto myself; that where I am, there ye may be also.
> — John 14:3, KJV

Read together, the three passages describe a personal return of Christ, a resurrection of believers who have died, a transformation of the body, and a permanent reunion.

## Who will be taken in the rapture?

Scripture describes those included as belonging to Christ. Paul's phrase is "the dead in Christ," and he addresses the living believers he is writing to as included with them. The dividing line in the text is relationship to Christ, not nationality, church membership, or personal achievement.

Christians across traditions agree on that much. Beyond it, questions such as whether some believers could be excluded through unreadiness are matters of interpretation on which sincere Christians differ, and the passages above do not settle them directly.

## When will the rapture happen?

No one knows, and Scripture states this plainly rather than leaving it open:

> But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.
> — Matthew 24:36, KJV

Jesus adds that the Son of man comes at an hour when He is not expected (Matthew 24:44), and Paul writes that the day of the Lord comes as a thief in the night (1 Thessalonians 5:2). Every date that has ever been set for this event has passed without incident, which is the outcome the texts themselves predict.

What Scripture does encourage is watchfulness — an attentive readiness that does not depend on knowing when. The delay itself has a name in Scripture: the patience of God, which Peter says is time given for repentance rather than evidence of indifference. That is the subject of a separate piece on [why God allows suffering to continue](/articles/why-does-god-allow-suffering).

::note Where Christians disagree
:: The timing of the rapture in relation to the tribulation and the second coming is one of the most debated questions in Christian theology. Some hold that believers are taken before a period of tribulation, others during or after it, and others that the passages above describe the second coming itself rather than a separate earlier event. These positions are interpretations built on the same texts. This article sets out what the passages say; it does not attempt to settle the debate.

The distinction between the two events, and where the two are held apart in Scripture, is set out in [the rapture or the second coming — what is the difference?](/articles/rapture-or-second-coming-what-is-the-difference)

## What does Prophet Dr. David Owuor teach about the rapture?

Prophet Dr. David Edward Owuor is the founder and leader of the Ministry of Repentance and Holiness, a Kenyan Christian ministry whose stated vision is to prepare the way for the coming of the Messiah. The rapture is central to that stated purpose rather than a secondary theme.

According to the ministry's published teaching, the rapture will occur suddenly and without warning, in the manner the passages above describe: a loud command, the voice of the archangel, the trumpet of God, the resurrection of believers who have died, and the catching up of those still living. The ministry teaches that believers will receive glorified bodies at that moment, following 1 Corinthians 15.

According to Prophet Dr. David Owuor, the decisive issue is readiness rather than information. His teaching consistently ties the rapture to repentance and holiness — that the event is for those genuinely born again and living holy lives, and that preparation is therefore a present matter of how a person lives rather than a future matter of calculating a date. In common with the passage in Matthew 24, his teaching maintains that the exact day and hour are not known.

The recording sits in the ministry's [teaching archive](/teachings/promise-of-glorification) with the rest of the series.

::note Ministry teaching, not plain text
:: The paragraphs above describe what the Ministry of Repentance and Holiness teaches. They are summarised rather than quoted, and they should be read as the ministry's position on these passages rather than as statements the biblical text makes directly. Readers wanting the teaching in its own words should consult the ministry's official channels.

## How should Christians prepare for the rapture?

Scripture answers this consistently: by being ready now, not by working out when. Five themes recur.

- **Faith in Christ** — the passages describe those who belong to Him, which is where readiness begins.
- **Repentance** — turning from sin rather than intending to.
- **Holiness** — a life set apart for God, which Hebrews 12:14 links directly to seeing the Lord. What that verse does and does not require is set out in [without holiness no man shall see the Lord](/articles/what-does-without-holiness-no-man-shall-see-the-lord-mean).
- **Watchfulness** — Jesus repeatedly told His followers to watch, precisely because the time is unknown (Matthew 24:42).
- **Faithfulness** — in the parable that follows, the servant commended is the one found doing his work when his master returns (Matthew 24:46).

None of these requires knowing the date. That is the point of them.

## What the rapture means for a Christian

The rapture is presented in Scripture as comfort rather than threat. Paul's stated reason for describing it was so that believers grieving the death of other Christians would not sorrow as those without hope (1 Thessalonians 4:13), and he ends the passage by telling them to comfort one another with these words (1 Thessalonians 4:18).

That is also where the practical emphasis of the Ministry of Repentance and Holiness rests. Its call to repentance and holiness is not framed as a way to work out the timing, but as the way to be found ready whenever it comes — which is the one instruction every position in the debate holds in common.

## Sources

Scripture quotations are from the King James Version, which is in the public domain. Statements describing the teaching of the Ministry of Repentance and Holiness and of Prophet Dr. David Edward Owuor are summarised from the ministry's own published material and are not direct quotations.

?? What is the rapture of the church?
?: It is the event described in 1 Thessalonians 4:16-17, in which the Lord descends from heaven, the dead in Christ rise first, and believers who are still alive are caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air. Paul adds in 1 Corinthians 15:51-52 that the body is changed in a moment at the last trump.

?? Is the word "rapture" in the Bible?
?: No. The English word comes from raptura, related to the Latin verb used in the fourth-century Vulgate rendering of 1 Thessalonians 4:17, which translates the Greek harpazo — to seize, snatch, or carry off suddenly. The same Greek verb describes Philip being caught away in Acts 8:39. The term is a description drawn from the passage rather than a title Scripture uses.

?? When will the rapture happen?
?: Scripture states that no one knows. Matthew 24:36 says that of that day and hour knows no man, not the angels of heaven, but the Father only. Jesus adds that the Son of man comes at an hour when He is not expected (Matthew 24:44), and Paul writes that the day of the Lord comes as a thief in the night (1 Thessalonians 5:2). Every date ever set for it has passed without incident.

?? Who will be taken in the rapture?
?: Paul describes those included as belonging to Christ — "the dead in Christ" together with the living believers he is writing to. The dividing line in the text is relationship to Christ rather than nationality, church membership, or personal achievement. Whether some believers could be excluded through unreadiness is a question on which sincere Christians differ.

?? Does the rapture happen before or after the tribulation?
?: This is one of the most debated questions in Christian theology. Some hold that believers are taken before a period of tribulation, others during or after it, and others that these passages describe the second coming itself rather than a separate earlier event. All of these are interpretations built on the same texts, and the passages do not settle the question directly.

?? What happens to believers who have already died?
?: 1 Thessalonians 4:16 says the dead in Christ rise first, before living believers are caught up. Paul's stated reason for describing the event at all was so that Christians grieving other Christians would not sorrow as those who have no hope (1 Thessalonians 4:13), and he closes by telling them to comfort one another with these words (1 Thessalonians 4:18).

?? What does Prophet Dr. David Owuor teach about the rapture?
?: According to the Ministry of Repentance and Holiness, the rapture will occur suddenly and without warning, with a loud command, the voice of the archangel and the trumpet of God, and believers will receive glorified bodies at that moment following 1 Corinthians 15. Its teaching ties the rapture to repentance and holiness, holding that the decisive issue is present readiness rather than knowledge of the timing, and that the day and hour are not known.

?? How should a Christian prepare for the rapture?
?: Scripture's answer is readiness now rather than calculation. Faith in Christ, repentance from sin, holiness — which Hebrews 12:14 links directly to seeing the Lord — watchfulness, because the time is unknown (Matthew 24:42), and faithfulness in ordinary work, since the servant commended is the one found doing it when his master returns (Matthew 24:46). None of these requires knowing the date.
